questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- Reputation of host university
- Subjective attractiveness of host country
- Number of available places

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: - Easy to navigate, as a lot of information was provided (often multiple times)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: - Choosing graduate courses, as it is a manual process due to the exchange and cannot be done by oneself. Rather, I had to go to the graduate office, where someone had to register me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Tartu College, apply as early as their application period opens. Directly next to campus and affordable.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I was only technically off-campus. Practically, the campus started across the street. Try to get as close as possible to the campus, then you can walk everywhere.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Unfortunately I did not get the courses I had hoped for, as they were already full.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Manually in the graduate office

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Personal help from the employee at the office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not successful, as other full-time students could register earlier.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contact the graduate office immediately, even show up in their consultation hours.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Pretty comparable in terms of difficulty. More research-based project work with your own chosen project. Smaller courses, more school-like feel.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lectures are very comparable to UCPH. However, the type of assignments are different, in one course only two over the semester, in the other none. Also, there were no exams, only project reports and a poster presentation in one of the courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Computational Imaging
Topics in Storage Systems
Algorithms for Private Data Analysis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Computational Imaging is a great introductory course with a lot to learn. Also, there is a project in which you can choose the topic on your own.

questions.answer: Groceries are more expensive. In general, the cost of living is slightly higher than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports clubs, introduction events, student committee organised parties

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the introductory events, also organised via Facebook. Great way to meet people at the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Drive to Algonquin National Park
Fly to Banff National Park
Go to Toronto Islands
See sports games (University ones are for free)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sports clubs. Otherwise, in the courses it was not as easy to socialize with others.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Competitive culture in class.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Diversity and positive attitude.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Apply early for housing, as it can be expensive and far-off if you apply too late.
- Try to see as much as possible in the city, go to games of sports you have never seen before, join clubs to socialize with Canadians.
- Studying is even more self-responsible than UCPH, try to allocate your time accordingly.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
- Meeting a lot of new people, some of which have become good friends
- Experiencing the life in a really big city and the differences to Copenhagen

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: - Organise and manage in the beginning, settling in, furnishing the student room

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
